changeHypothesis.summary: Infrastructure/replacement demand and industry research supported a multi-quarter construction-machinery recovery. Sany and Zoomlion had low forward valuations and quantified earnings paths, but the frozen equity basket was still materially adverse relative to CSI300.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: Replacement cycle, market-share concentration and infrastructure activity can persist across multiple reporting periods.
disconfirmingEvidence: Both frozen machinery names underperformed CSI300 over 20d and 60d.
Sany Q1 earnings were still sharply down.
The recovery forecast could already assume a large post-lockdown normalization.

causalChain.mechanism: Construction activity and replacement demand lift excavator/crane sales.
Higher volumes and concentration improve operating leverage and profit.
causalChain.failureMode: price competition or Q1 weakness persists

falseThemeMatches: broad industrial names without machinery sales exposure

selectionComparison.rationale: Both direct expressions are acceptable; Sany is preferred for the clearer quantified operating-leverage thesis, not because it must outperform Zoomlion.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: Forecasts already expected Sany +28.8% 2020 profit and low-teens/low-double-digit PE, while both stocks still lagged CSI300 over 20d and 60d.
expectations.thesisExpectation: If replacement and infrastructure demand persist, earnings can exceed the conservative outer-year path and the adverse price regime may reverse.
expectations.measurableGap: Fundamentals/valuation look more constructive than price confirmation, so this remains Research rather than Primary.

expectationBurdenTest.valuationMethod: Forward earnings and normalized machinery-cycle PE.
expectationBurdenTest.marketBaseline: Sany 2020/21/22 profit +28.8%/+15.2%/+6.2% at ~10.9x/9.4x/8.9x PE; Zoomlion similarly low PE.
expectationBurdenTest.thesisScenario: Demand persistence/share gains lift earnings above the frozen baseline and relative price begins to confirm.
expectationBurdenTest.breakevenCondition: Recovery must produce earnings revisions rather than just meet already-positive forecasts.
expectationBurdenTest.ordinaryScenarioFailure: Industry rebound is temporary and stocks remain value traps despite low multiples.
expectationBurdenTest.catalystOrTimingBridge: H1/Q3 results and monthly machinery demand can test the thesis.

fundamentalAcceleration.rationale: Industrial profits and infrastructure-linked demand were improving by late Q2.

realizedCompanyConfirmation.rationale: Zoomlion stayed profitable but Sany Q1 earnings were still sharply down; the full rebound had not been reported.

crossSectionalConfirmation.rationale: The price basket was adverse with zero positive relative breadth.

baselineLag.rationale: Late-June forecasts explicitly quantified a positive but slowing multi-year earnings path.

priceAbsorption.checkMethod: Both names lagged CSI300 over 20d and 60d, so price absorption is low rather than high.

priceRegime.method: equal-weight frozen opportunity basket versus CSI300 using hfq history

fundamentalImpulse.rationale: Post-lockdown industrial/infrastructure activity and machinery forecasts point to accelerating recovery.

earningsRevisionBreadth.rationale: Both Sany and Zoomlion carried positive forward earnings paths in late-June research.

eventHalfLife.rationale: Replacement and infrastructure demand can persist through multiple quarters.

lateCycleRisk.rationale: Stocks had not rerated relative to CSI300 despite improving expectations.

opportunityTimingTest.rationale: Fundamentals and valuation are constructive, but V1.3 correctly refuses Primary status while the broad pre-cutoff equity regime remains adverse.

qualityFloor.rationale: Sany Q1 was weak, while Zoomlion remained profitable; recovery quality was not uniformly realized.

revisionHeadroom.rationale: Late-June research quantified strong 2020 recovery and continued 2021 growth.

valuationSlack.rationale: Forward PE was around high single digits to low double digits.

catalystReachability.rationale: H1/Q3 earnings and machinery sales are near-term tests.

downsideContainment.rationale: Low valuation and profitable leaders provide some containment, though a cyclical slowdown can still hurt.

earningsConversionBridge.driverChange: Infrastructure/replacement demand was expected to lift construction-machinery volumes after Q1 disruption.
earningsConversionBridge.earningsMechanism: Higher machinery volumes and market share improve manufacturer revenue and operating leverage.
earningsConversionBridge.nextObservableMetric: H1/Q3 machinery sales, revenue and profit
earningsConversionBridge.failureCondition: H1/Q3 earnings fail to accelerate despite the demand recovery.

baselinePath.nearTerm: Sany Q1 profit -31.9%, Zoomlion Q1 roughly flat-positive.
baselinePath.nextPeriod: 2020 forecasts embed strong recovery, especially Sany +28.8% profit.
baselinePath.laterPeriod: 2021-22 growth slows materially in the published path.
baselinePath.rationale: Late-June forecasts already assume a recovery but not indefinite acceleration.

thesisPath.nearTermChange: Q2/H1 demand can reverse the Q1 earnings weakness.
thesisPath.nextPeriodChange: 2020 results can exceed the recovery baseline if replacement/share gains persist.
thesisPath.laterPeriodChange: Outer-year growth can stay above the slowing baseline if concentration and replacement demand last.
thesisPath.mechanism: The gap is duration and conversion of the post-lockdown recovery, not simply low PE.

incrementalPathAdvantage.rationale: The post-Q1 demand recovery can improve the path beyond already-positive forecasts.

durationRisk.rationale: Cyclical normalization is real, but low valuation reduces long-duration burden.

expectationPathTest.falsifier: H1/Q3 earnings do not improve materially and relative price remains adverse despite strong industry demand.
